name: CHI
fullName: ACM Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
notes: Main papers track. No separate abstract deadline. Submission includes videos and supplementary materials. The official 24-hour contingency grace period is not included in the deadline shown. Notification times are not specified.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

paperFit.emphasis: User studies, human needs and task outcomes

guide.contribution: Interaction techniques, tools and findings about human needs, behavior or experience. A contribution can be a new interface evaluated with users, an empirical study, or design knowledge grounded in interviews, observation or deployment. Explain what changes for the intended users and why.
guide.evidence: Human-centered contributions usually need direct evidence from users: controlled user studies, interviews, observation or field deployments. For interface comparisons, measure task performance and experience against relevant alternatives. For qualitative work, explain recruitment, analysis and how the findings support the design conclusions.

comparisons.difference: CHI connects an interface to user needs and activities, using interviews, task studies or deployment. IEEE VR more directly tests immersive effects such as embodiment, presence, comfort and performance inside a virtual environment.

CHI studies interfaces across activities such as communication, input and creative work. HRI focuses on people working with robots, testing how autonomy, physical assistance and robot communication affect performance and trust.

name: IEEE VR
fullName: IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces
notes: One unified submission and review process for IEEE TVCG and conference-only papers. A paper abstract is required seven days before the paper. Notification times are not specified.

journals: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (TVCG)
publication.note: Unified review assigns accepted papers to the journal or conference proceedings.

paperFit.scope: Immersive interaction, embodiment and VR systems
paperFit.emphasis: User studies for interaction and experience

guide.contribution: Immersive interaction techniques, systems and findings about presence, embodiment, locomotion or social behavior. For an interaction contribution, establish how the technique changes what people can do or experience. Technical contributions also advance tracking, rendering and displays across VR, AR and MR.
guide.evidence: Plan a user study for claims about interaction, presence, embodiment, comfort or usability. Compare relevant techniques with participants, measuring task performance and appropriate subjective responses. For tracking, rendering or system contributions, use accuracy, latency, image-quality or throughput benchmarks; add a user study when claiming a perceptual or experiential benefit.

comparisons.difference: IEEE VR and ISMAR are very similar. IEEE VR has a stronger emphasis on immersive interaction, locomotion, avatars, presence and embodiment. ISMAR has an AR/MR emphasis: aligning and blending virtual content with physical environments, including tracking, displays and spatial interaction. User studies and technical XR systems fit both.

IEEE VR and ACM SAP both study perception with human participants. ACM SAP specializes in perceptual mechanisms, such as sensitivity to motion or rendering changes; IEEE VR also evaluates complete immersive tasks and systems.

name: ISMAR
fullName: IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality
notes: Unified IEEE TVCG journal and conference paper track. The 2027 site confirms Kobe, Japan, but the conference dates and paper deadlines are still TBA; estimates use the verified 2026 schedule.

journals: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (TVCG)
publication.note: Unified review assigns accepted papers to the journal or conference proceedings.

paperFit.scope: AR/MR integration, spatial interaction and XR systems
paperFit.emphasis: User studies for interaction and experience

guide.contribution: AR/MR techniques and systems that align, blend or connect virtual content with physical environments: tracking, displays, scene reconstruction and spatial interaction. Contributions also cover VR and human experience. For an interaction contribution, connect the design to a measurable change in user performance or perception.
guide.evidence: Plan a user study for interaction, usability or perceptual claims. Compare techniques with participants using task accuracy, completion time, workload, comfort or experience measures. For sensing, tracking and reconstruction contributions, benchmark accuracy, robustness and latency; use participants to substantiate any claimed improvement in user experience.

comparisons.difference: ISMAR and IEEE VR are very similar. ISMAR has a stronger AR/MR emphasis, including registration, real–virtual compositing, displays and interaction with physical surroundings. IEEE VR emphasizes immersive interaction, locomotion, avatars, presence and embodiment. Both publish across AR, VR and MR and use user studies for human-experience claims.

ISMAR and IEEE AIxVR overlap in AI-enabled immersive systems. IEEE AIxVR centers the AI method or adaptation; ISMAR also covers interfaces and XR technology without AI. In both, claims about better user performance or experience call for a user study.

name: VRST
fullName: ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology
notes: Main papers track. The abstract is required one week before the full paper. Includes the officially extended revision and final-notification dates. No official 2027 schedule was found. Notification times are not specified.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: VR hardware, input techniques and systems that improve interaction, alongside empirical findings about their use. Show how a device or technique changes the user task. Algorithmic contributions can focus on recognition, tracking or computational efficiency within a VR system.
guide.evidence: Use a comparative user study for input techniques and usability claims, measuring task completion, accuracy, workload and experience. For computational components, compare benchmark accuracy, runtime and resource use, with ablations. Evaluate the component with users when the claimed benefit concerns interaction rather than computational performance.

comparisons.difference: VRST and IEEE VR are very similar for VR interaction, input devices and systems. Both use participant studies to evaluate interaction and user experience, and benchmarks to evaluate technical components.

VRST and CHI both publish interaction techniques evaluated with users. VRST focuses on VR technology and tasks; CHI also covers broader human activities, design research and experiences outside immersive environments.

name: ACM SAP
notes: Abstract submission is required. The paper deadline was extended from April 28. This schedule covers SAP proceedings papers; invited TAP journal papers have a separate second review and final deadline. Notification release has no exact time.

publication.note: Selected papers undergo a second review cycle and publish in TAP instead of the proceedings.

paperFit.scope: Perception of graphics and virtual humans

guide.contribution: Findings and models about human perception of graphics, animation and multisensory content. Isolate a perceptual question, such as sensitivity to motion, expression or rendering changes, and explain what the result means for visual presentation or interaction design.
guide.evidence: Controlled perceptual experiments with human participants are central. Manipulate the stimulus and measure judgments, discrimination thresholds, gaze or response time. Use an appropriate experimental design and statistical analysis to connect the observed effect to the changed stimulus; validate perceptual models against human responses.

comparisons.difference: ACM SAP isolates how a stimulus changes perception, using controlled judgments, eye tracking or detection thresholds. IEEE VR tests how such changes affect an immersive task, including performance, presence and comfort.

ACM SAP studies how people perceive expressions, motion and sensory cues. ACM IVA develops the agent behavior behind an interaction, testing dialogue consistency, believability and negotiation or training outcomes.

name: IEEE AIxVR
fullName: IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and eXtended and Virtual Reality
notes: Formerly IEEE AIVR; renamed AIxVR in 2024. This schedule covers full/short papers, extended from September 17 to September 21, 2026. Notifications are only specified as early-to-mid-November 2026, so no exact notification date is shown. Separate 2027 work-in-progress and demo/video tracks close October 29, 2026; workshops set their own deadlines. The source states AoE but gives no exact clock time.

core.note: No matching entry found by acronym and full title; this is not an Unranked classification.

publication.note: Selected papers are invited to submit extended versions; the 2027 call does not name the journal.

paperFit.emphasis: AI benchmarks and user studies for adaptation

guide.contribution: AI methods and adaptive systems for XR, including prediction, sensing and personalized training. Explain the improvement to the model or system. For adaptive interaction, connect the adaptation to a measurable change in user performance, workload or experience.
guide.evidence: Benchmark model accuracy, robustness, latency and resource use against alternatives. For personalized training or adaptive interaction, use a user study comparing adaptation with a fixed or conventional system. Measure learning or task performance alongside workload and experience, according to the claimed benefit.

comparisons.difference: IEEE AIxVR tests AI-based prediction and adaptation in XR, including robustness to calibration errors and effects on training. ISMAR also includes scene capture and spatial interfaces evaluated through reconstruction quality and task performance.

IEEE AIxVR applies learning to XR sensing and adaptation, measuring prediction accuracy, workload or training performance. ACM IVA focuses on social agents, measuring consistency across conversations, believability and interaction outcomes.

name: ACM IVA
fullName: ACM International Conference on Intelligent Virtual Agents
notes: Full papers track with a separate abstract deadline. Submission dates include the published extensions; these extensions may not recur. The IVA series announces Reykjavik in September 2027, but exact event dates and paper deadlines are not published; estimates use the 2026 schedule. Notification times are not specified.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

paperFit.emphasis: User studies of agent behavior and interaction

guide.contribution: Agent architectures, expressive behaviors and findings about human–agent interaction. Contributions can improve dialogue or behavioral consistency, or explain how an agent affects people. Claims about believability, engagement or social behavior should connect the agent design to human responses.
guide.evidence: Use user studies for claims about believability, trust, engagement or social interaction, comparing agent behaviors with participants. Measure task outcomes and subjective responses. Algorithmic contributions also need benchmarks for behavior generation or dialogue consistency; evaluate extended interactions when claiming sustained coherence.

comparisons.difference: ACM IVA develops agent reasoning and responses, evaluating dialogue consistency, negotiation and believability. ACM SAP studies perception of the resulting presentation, using controlled changes to expressions, motion or sensory cues.

ACM IVA studies conversational architectures and adaptive social behavior. HRI also studies physical robot assistance and shared autonomy, where task completion, cognitive load and trust in the robot become central outcomes.

name: HRI
fullName: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction
topics: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction
notes: Full papers track. Short contributions and alt.HRI have separate deadlines. Late-breaking reports close December 8, 2026; videos and demos close November 20. These are distinct from the main full-paper track shown here.

publication.note: Nominated papers needing further work may transfer for continued journal review. This is not automatic journal publication.

paperFit.emphasis: User studies and human–robot task outcomes

guide.contribution: Robot interfaces, collaborative behaviors and findings about how people work with robots. Contributions may develop a new interaction or explain human needs and behavior through empirical research. Connect autonomy, assistance or communication to the human partner’s task and experience.
guide.evidence: Human–robot interaction claims generally need evidence from participants: controlled user studies, interviews or field studies with intended users. Measure task success, workload, trust or communication as appropriate. Hardware and autonomy benchmarks support technical claims; participant evidence establishes the effect on people.

comparisons.difference: HRI tests how robot autonomy and physical assistance affect people, measuring task performance, workload and trust. CHI covers a wider range of interfaces and activities, often combining user research with task studies or deployment.

HRI work studies assistive manipulation and robot communication in physical settings. ACM IVA focuses on how agents reason and converse, testing behavioral consistency, believability and negotiation outcomes.
